title: Hosted API: soft-decline admission & predictive capacity fill — post-incident action plan
creator: Ava Morales
description: Follow-up ticket created after a hosted API GPU exhaustion event where large tenant bursts caused queue amplification and prolonged soft-failure for many customers. This ticket bundles telemetry gaps, short-term mitigations, and medium-term runtime changes to make admission and scaling behaviour degrade gracefully rather than causing systemic queue buildup.
incident_summary: On 2025-03-08, a combination of simultaneous large-batch requests and a delayed autoscaler ramp produced persistent GPU pool exhaustion. Symptoms: increasing queued request length, priority inversion for small requests, rapid token throttles, and repeated scale thrash as autoscaler attempted aggressive priming then backed off due to hysteresis. Impact: several enterprise customers experienced elevated latency and ~15% increased error rates for 47 minutes before manual containment.
root_cause: Primary causes identified: (1) admission policy allowed prefetching tenants to occupy slots disproportionally during burst; (2) autoscaler tuning had insufficient predictive headroom and aggressive cooldown leading to oscillation; (3) telemetry lacked an early composite signal combining queue growth rate + per-tenant slot occupancy to trigger soft-decline; (4) tenant credit scoring amplified bursty tenants because short-lived small requests were deprioritized under the same credit buckets.
mitigation_taken: Immediate steps during the incident: (1) emergency soft-decline rollout to reduce allowed inflight requests per tenant by 30%; (2) manual priming of standby machines for the affected region; (3) temporary tenant-level caps for top 3 noisy tenants; (4) increased autoscaler target headroom to 20% while the team stabilized queues.
analysis_and_observations: Post-incident analysis showed that prefix/KV cache reuse was low for the burst traffic, so batching benefits were limited. The queue growth curve was superlinear once tenant occupancy exceeded 65% of pool capacity. Our current admission signals are per-request and do not capture momentum (queue growth rate), which delayed preemptive soft-decline. Observed fairness regressions: small interactive requests experienced 2x latency amplification when large-batch requests surged. Autoscaler logs show repeated scale-up then scale-down within 5–7 minute windows due to cooldown/hysteresis configuration.
decision_records: Adopt a graduated soft-decline admission policy that reacts to composite signals (pool_queue_growth_rate, tenant_slot_share, tail_latency_p50_p95 ratio).

Implement a short-term predictive priming window in the autoscaler: when queue_growth_rate exceeds threshold for 60s, provision a small burst of capacity (2-4 nodes) without resetting cooldown counters.
Separate tenant credit buckets for large-batch vs interactive workloads to prevent priority inversion.
Improve telemetry: add composite 'pressure' metric and a per-tenant slot-occupancy time-series with 1s granularity to Console dashboards and alerts.
action_items: (A1) Telemetry: instrument composite pool_pressure = weighted(queue_growth_rate, tenant_slot_share, avg_token_rate). Owner: SRE (Liam). ETA: 2025-03-22.
(A2) Admission: implement graduated soft-decline glue that can apply mild throttles (10-40%) by tenant based on pool_pressure. Owner: Serving Runtime (Priya). ETA: 2025-03-29.
(A3) Autoscaler: add 'predictive_priming' mode which can allocate a configurable burst (2-6 nodes) when pressure persists for configurable window. Owner: Autoscale Team (Noah). ETA: 2025-04-05.
(A4) Runtime fairness: split credit buckets into 'interactive' and 'batch' classes; update admission scoring. Owner: Runtime Scheduling (Chen). ETA: 2025-04-12.
(A5) Runbooks: update hosted capacity runbook with new soft-decline play, step-by-step containment, and tenant cap checklist. Owner: SRE Ops (Marta). ETA: 2025-03-20.
(A6) E2E test: create synthetic tenant-storm test that validates autoscaler priming and admission soft-decline in CI. Owner: Test Infra (Diego). ETA: 2025-04-02.
(A7) Dashboard: add a pre-incident alert (P0) based on sustained pool_pressure > 0.7 for 45s. Owner: Observability (Harper). ETA: 2025-03-18.
(A8) Customer comms: notify affected tenants with incident summary and mitigation, and offer review meeting. Owner: CS (Elena). ETA: 2025-03-14.
acceptance_criteria: Composite pool_pressure metric visible in Console and returns sane values during synthetic storm tests.
Soft-decline policy can be toggled via feature-flag and reduces queue growth slope by >= 30% in experiments.
Predictive priming reduces mean time to steady-state throughput during synthetic surges by >= 40% compared to baseline.
No regression to p99 latency for interactive workloads in staged canary (<=5% delta).
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: overly aggressive soft-decline may increase client 429s and surface as 'throttling' to tenants. Mitigation: phased rollout with feature-flag, telemetry-backed thresholds, customer-facing metrics and a 2-week canary against low-risk pools. Risk: predictive priming could overshoot capacity causing cost spike — mitigation: cap priming to 5% of pool and track cost delta in Console.
